facts.text: The dusky moorhen has a red frontal shield and a yellow-tipped red bill, with orange-yellow legs.
facts.quote: It has a red frontal shield and yellow-tipped red bill like its Eurasian relative, but lacks the white flank line shown by common moorhen, and has orange-yellow rather than yellow legs.

facts.text: Its territorial call can be heard from over two kilometres away as birds in nearby territories take it up.
facts.quote: This call is taken up by birds in surrounding territories and can be heard from over two kilometres away.

facts.text: Both sexes make a soft mewing noise, or a soft kook noise, before and during courtship.
facts.quote: Both sexes make a soft mewing noise, or a soft kook noise before and during courtship.

facts.text: Chicks are fed mostly on annelid worms and molluscs, with plant matter added as they mature.
facts.quote: The chicks are fed mostly on annelid worms and molluscs, with plant matter gradually being given in increasing proportions by the parents as the young mature.

facts.text: In southern Australia it breeds from August to January, usually raising a single brood.
facts.quote: Breeding season is from August to January in the south of Australia, with generally one brood, and January to June in the north, often brooding twice.

facts.text: It often flicks its conspicuous white and black tail, possibly signalling alertness or social status.
facts.quote: The moorhens frequently flick their conspicuous white and black tail. This may be a signal of alertness or of social status, depending on the context.

facts.text: The dusky moorhen prefers freshwater marshes and swamps and is rarely found far from them.
facts.quote: The dusky moorhen is found in wetland habitats, with a preference for freshwater marshes and swamps, and are rarely found far from these areas except when foraging in nearby vegetation.

facts.text: These birds rarely migrate far and may stay in the same location for eight years or more.
facts.quote: The birds do not often migrate long distances, and may remain in the same location for eight years or more.

facts.text: Its species name comes from the Latin tenebrosa, meaning dark.
facts.quote: Its species name is derived from the Latin tenebrosa "dark".
